description: Cut the fixed prepare() overhead without touching training numerics. Base: E069 (commit 5ed8687). Background: I102 showed that reruns of E069 are bit-identical on seeds 0-2. Prepare took 0.152/0.146/0.062 s on trials 0/1/2 (mean ~0.12 s, ~2.5% of the score), so trials 0-1 pay ~0.09 s of first-use cost. Gate in drafts/, untimed. Instrument prepare() per component on each of 3 consecutive trials in one process, using cuda-synchronized timers: file read/unpickle, label conversion, H2D copy, uint8 buffer setup, whitening fit (covariance, then eigh or whatever the code uses), parameter/buffer/optimizer/lookahead/Muon-buffer reset, and generator seeding. Launch only if the trial-0/1 excess plus any removable steady-state cost is >=0.05 s per trial on average. Change (all in build() on synthetic inputs, never real data or seeds): (1) Run the whitening-fit linear algebra once on a synthetic covariance of the exact shape, dtype and device. This initializes the cuSOLVER/cuBLAS handles and workspaces before the timed region. (2) Allocate and free synthetic tensors of the exact sizes prepare() and train() create: the on-GPU uint8 train set, labels, the per-epoch augmented and resized buffers at 20/28/32 px, and the permutation. The caching allocator then already holds those blocks. (3) Allocate an empty pinned host staging buffer of the train-set size. prepare() reads the real data into it and does a non_blocking H2D copy, with a sync before the whitening fit. Leave every arithmetic op, the RNG order and the data order unchanged. Before launching, rerun offline on seeds 0-2 and require per-seed accuracy bit-identical to E069 (0.7578/0.7535/0.7569). Also log per-trial prepare times.
